title: Go Flyers - Test 1 - Speaking
source: Go Flyers Teacher's Notes - Key to tests - Test 1 - Speaking (pp. 17-19)

teacher_name.description: Choose a short friendly English teacher name and keep it consistent for the whole session.

session_rules.finish_policy: Continue until all parts and exchanges are completed, unless the user ends the session early.

instructions: Usher brings the student in.
Examiner greets the student and asks opening personal questions.
parts.notes: Based on p.17 speaking opening lines.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: Hello. My name's {{teacher_name}}.

expected_child_response.description: The child should greet the examiner and say their first name.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: Hello. / My name is ... / I am ...
expected_child_response.notes: The greeting and name may happen across two short turns.

follow_ups: Please say your full name.
Can you answer in a full sentence?
exchanges.notes: Merged greeting + name setup into one structured exchange.

priority_answer.text: Hello.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: If there is no official or source reference answer, generate a short A2-level full sentence that matches the target pattern.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: What's your surname?

expected_child_response.description: The child should say their surname or family name.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: My surname is ... / My family name is ...
expected_child_response.notes: Source includes both surname and family name prompts.

follow_ups: Please say it in a full sentence.

priority_answer.instruction: Use the child's real surname or family name as the answer content.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the child's real surname or family name as the answer content.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: How old are you?

expected_child_response.description: The child should say their age, then answer the yes/no check question.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: I am ... years old. / Yes, I am. / No, I am not.
expected_child_response.notes: There may be two short responses in sequence.

follow_ups: Please answer in a full sentence.

priority_answer.instruction: Use the child's real age as the answer content.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the child's real age as the answer content.

instructions: Show the student both Find the differences cards.
Here are two pictures. My picture is similar to yours, but there are some differences.
For example, in my picture there's a girl on a rock in the lake, but in your picture there isn't.
I will say something about my picture. Can you tell me how your picture is different?
parts.notes: Student looks at printed picture. Model does not see image.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: In my picture, two boys are sitting under a tree.
exchanges.student_reference: In my picture, two girls are sitting under a tree.
exchanges.follow_up_question: Who is sitting under a tree in your picture?

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe the difference using a full sentence about the people under the tree.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: In my picture, ... are sitting under a tree.
expected_child_response.notes: Information depends on the child's card.

follow_ups: Please say the full sentence.
Who is sitting under the tree in your picture?

priority_answer.text: In my picture, two girls are sitting under a tree.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the fixed card-based answer. Do not freely change the core information.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: In my picture, the woman is eating a sandwich.
exchanges.student_reference: In my picture, the woman is eating pizza.

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe what the woman is eating in their picture.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: In my picture, the woman is eating ...

follow_ups: Say the full sentence, please.
What is the woman eating in your picture?

priority_answer.text: In my picture, the woman is eating pizza.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the fixed card-based answer. Do not freely change the core information.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: In my picture, there isn't a pizza on the blanket.
exchanges.student_reference: In my picture there is a pizza on the blanket.

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe the item on the blanket in their picture.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: In my picture, there is ... on the blanket.

follow_ups: Please say the whole sentence.
What's on the blanket in your picture?

priority_answer.text: In my picture there is a pizza on the blanket.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the fixed card-based answer. Do not freely change the core information.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: In my picture, two boys are riding their bikes.
exchanges.student_reference: In my picture, one boy is riding his bike.
exchanges.follow_up_question: How many boys are riding their bikes?

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe how many boys are riding bikes in their picture.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: In my picture, ... boy(s) ... riding ... bike(s).

follow_ups: Say the full sentence, please.
How many boys are riding bikes in your picture?

priority_answer.text: In my picture, one boy is riding his bike.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the fixed card-based answer. Do not freely change the core information.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: In my picture, a man is reading a newspaper outside the tent.
exchanges.student_reference: In my picture, a man is reading a magazine outside the tent.
exchanges.follow_up_question: What is the man outside the tent reading?

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe what the man is reading in their picture.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: In my picture, a man is reading ... outside the tent.

follow_ups: Please say the full sentence.
What is the man reading in your picture?

priority_answer.text: In my picture, a man is reading a magazine outside the tent.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the fixed card-based answer. Do not freely change the core information.

questions: Repeat what the student has to do.
Who is sitting under a tree in your picture?
How many boys are riding their bikes?
What is the man outside the tent reading?

instructions: Show the student the Information exchange cards.
Give the student his or her card.
Richard and Harry are friends. They go to school together.
I don't know anything about Richard's programme. So I'm going to ask you some questions.
Point to the box on the right of the student's card.
Ask the questions.
Now, you don't know anything about Harry's programme, so you ask me some questions.
Point to the box on the left of the student's card.
You can point to the information on your card if necessary.
parts.notes: Complete information-exchange content from p.18. First half: examiner asks about Richard. Second half: student asks about Harry.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: What time does he get up in the morning?

expected_child_response.description: The child should answer with the exact time from the card.
expected_child_response.notes: This is card-based information retrieval, not open free speaking.

follow_ups: Please answer with the time.
What time does he get up?

instructions: These pictures tell a story.
It's called 'Betty's visit to London'.
Look at the pictures first.
Now you tell the story.
parts.notes: Story frames are based on p.19 visible prompts.

story_frames.teacher_setup: Betty, her brother Fred and their parents visit London. They arrive there on Monday and they go for a walk. They see Big Ben.

expected_child_response.description: The child should begin the story using the first picture setup.
expected_child_response.notes: This is the story opening provided by the examiner.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Generate a short A2-level story sentence using the frame setup and support questions.

story_frames.teacher_setup: On Tuesday Betty and her family go shopping. They buy many presents and souvenirs.

expected_child_response.description: The child should continue the story using the second picture.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Generate a short A2-level story sentence using the frame setup and support questions.

story_frames.teacher_setup: On Wednesday Betty writes a postcard to her grandmother.

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe the third story picture.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Generate a short A2-level story sentence using the frame setup and support questions.

story_frames.teacher_setup: On Thursday the family visits the zoo. They see a lot of animals there. Betty is afraid of the snakes and her brother, Fred, laughs.
support_questions: Is Betty afraid of the snakes?

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe the zoo picture and key actions.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Generate a short A2-level story sentence using the frame setup and support questions.

story_frames.teacher_setup: On Friday they are at the airport. It is the last day in London. They have their bags with them. Betty's father takes pictures of the family.
support_questions: What have they got with them?

expected_child_response.description: The child should finish the story with the airport picture.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Generate a short A2-level story sentence using the frame setup and support questions.

questions: Is Betty afraid of the snakes?
What have they got with them?

instructions: Put the Tell the story card away and turn to the student.
Now let's talk about what you do in your free time.
parts.notes: Based on p.19 personal questions section.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: What do you do after school?

expected_child_response.description: The child should answer with a full sentence about after-school activities.

follow_ups: Please answer in a full sentence.
What do you do after school?

priority_answer.text: I do my homework.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: If there is no official or source reference answer, generate a short A2-level full sentence that matches the target pattern.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: How often do you go out with your friends?
exchanges.follow_up_question: Do you go out every day?

expected_child_response.description: The child should answer with a frequency expression.

follow_ups: How often?
Please answer with the frequency.

priority_answer.text: Three times a week.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: If there is no official or source reference answer, generate a short A2-level full sentence that matches the target pattern.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: What do you usually do at the weekend?

expected_child_response.description: The child should answer with a full sentence about weekend activities.

follow_ups: Please use a full sentence.
What do you usually do at the weekend?

priority_answer.text: I visit my grandparents.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: If there is no official or source reference answer, generate a short A2-level full sentence that matches the target pattern.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: Do you play any sports?

expected_child_response.description: The child should answer yes or no and may add the sport they play.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: Yes, I do. I play ... / No, I don't.

follow_ups: Please answer with a full sentence.
What sport do you play?

priority_answer.text: Yes. I play football.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: If there is no official or source reference answer, generate a short A2-level full sentence that matches the target pattern.
